title: Cap. IX: Garissoles Levi–Abraham parallel; concede without immediate imputation
pass_a_gloss: Head II: What then does Garissoles gather from Levi's being tithed? He says: as Abraham was the originative principle of the Levitical people, propagated from him by seminal relation, so Adam is the material principle of the whole human race as to natural generation. Therefore if the Apostle rightly said Levitical priests were tithed in Abraham because they were in his loins when Abraham paid tithes to Melchizedek, God's priest, it should seem neither strange nor unusual that all humans are said to have sinned in Adam and in him been ruined and damned, insofar as all were in the loins of him while he was sinning. Placeus asks what forbids him to concede that whole comparison while still denying the immediate imputation of Adam's first actual sin.
pass_b_english: II. But what does D. Garissoles gather from Levi's being tithed? "As," he says, "Abraham was the originative principle of the Levitical nation, which was propagated from him according to seminal relation, so also Adam is the material principle of the whole human race as far as natural generation is concerned. Therefore if the Apostle rightly said that the Levitical priests were tithed in Abraham because they were in his loins when Abraham paid tithes to Melchizedek, the priest of God, nothing strange or unusual ought to seem in the saying that all humans sinned in Adam and in him were ruined and damned, insofar as all were in the loins of him while he was sinning." What forbids me to grant this whole comparison, while still denying the immediate imputation of Adam's first actual sin?
source_text: II. Sed quid ex decimatione Levi colligit D. Garissolius? Sicut, inquit, Abrahamus originarium fuit principium Gentis Leviticae, quae secundum rationem seminalem ab eo propagata est, ita & Adam principium est materiale totius generis humani, quod ad generationem naturalem attinet. Itaque si recte dictum est ab Apostolo Leviticos sacerdotes decimatos fuisse in Abrahamo, quia in ejus lumbis erant, quando scilicet Abrahamus Dei sacerdoti Melchisedeco decimas persolvit; nihil mirum videri debet, aut inusitatum, quod dicuntur omnes homines peccasse in Adamo, & in eo perditi ac damnati fuisse, quatenus omnes in ejus peccantis lumbis fuerunt. Quid vetat me hoc totum concedere, negantem imputationem primi Adae peccati actualis immediatam?
